paper.title: Divide and Conquer: Reliable Multi-View Evidential Learning for Deepfake Detection

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1-5 and Appendix A (implementation, algorithm, efficiency, robustness, limitations)

claims.claim: A face-deepfake detector generalises better to unseen datasets and unseen manipulation methods if, besides a semantic view from an adapted vision-language encoder, it builds a separate artifact view that is forced to be orthogonal to the semantic feature, and combines the two views' evidence with an uncertainty-aware fusion rule rather than averaging. Supported only if, trained only on FaceForensics++, it has the highest video-level AUC of a dozen published detectors on each of six unseen deepfake datasets and the highest average over eight unseen face-swap methods; if a variant with two copies of the semantic view, and a variant whose artifact view is not made orthogonal, both score lower, so the gain is not just extra capacity; and if replacing the fusion rule by averaging or the evidential objective by cross-entropy also scores lower.
claims.decision_rule: Best AUC on each of 6 cross-dataset sets and best DF40 average vs 12 baselines; f_s+f_s and f_s+f_r variants lower; mean fusion and CE variants lower.

claims.claim: A deepfake detector that fuses semantic and artifact evidence with an evidential rule can say when it is likely to be wrong: its uncertainty is high mainly on the images it misclassifies, and it is better calibrated than the same detector trained to make deterministic predictions. Supported only if, on unseen datasets, misclassified images concentrate at high uncertainty while correct ones sit near zero; if discarding the most uncertain predictions raises accuracy steadily as more are discarded, more than for the deterministic baseline; and if expected calibration error is at most half that of the deterministic version on each test set.
claims.decision_rule: Errors concentrated at high u; monotone risk-coverage gains above baseline; ECE <= half of the cross-entropy baseline on each set.

experiments.text: Fix the training and evaluation protocol. Setup: train only on FaceForensics++ at c23 compression with the DeepfakeBench preprocessing; CLIP ViT-L/14 kept frozen with LoRA (rank 8) on its attention layers; augmentation with Gaussian blur, JPEG compression and colour jitter; AdamW, learning rate 1e-4, batch 128, 20 epochs, one A100. Report video-level AUC on two protocols: cross-dataset on six unseen sets (Celeb-DF v2, DFD, DFDC, DeeperForensics, WildDeepfake, Celeb-DF v3), and cross-manipulation on eight face-swap methods from DF40, which share the FaceForensics++ source footage so that only the forgery method changes.

Compare with twelve published detectors. Setup: F3Net, SPSL, SRM, CORE, RECCE, SBI, UCF, IID, LSDA, ProDet, Effort and GenD under the same training data. Result: highest AUC on every cross-dataset set: Celeb-DF v2 0.977, DFD 0.982, DFDC 0.882, DeeperForensics 0.993, WildDeepfake 0.911, Celeb-DF v3 0.886, average 0.939 against 0.923 for GenD and 0.907 for Effort; highest on every DF40 method, average 0.976 against 0.958 (GenD) and 0.940 (Effort), the largest margins on BlendFace (0.963 vs 0.935) and FaceDancer (0.972 vs 0.942).

Rule out that a second branch helps simply by adding capacity, and test the orthogonality step. Setup: on Celeb-DF v2, DFDC and MobileFaceSwap, compare the semantic view alone, two copies of the semantic view, semantic view plus the raw residual (semantic feature minus its VAE reconstruction) without projection, and semantic view plus the residual projected orthogonal to the semantic feature. Result: averages 0.905, 0.917, 0.922 and 0.938, so duplicating the semantic view gains less than adding the residual, and the projection adds a further 1.6 points. Cross-correlation heatmaps show strong structured correlation between semantic features and raw residuals that the projection largely removes.

Test the fusion rule and the training objective. Setup: on the same three test sets, replace evidential learning with cross-entropy and mean fusion; keep evidential outputs but average the two views' belief masses; and use Dempster-Shafer combination, which raises uncertainty when the views conflict. Separately remove the cosine alignment loss or the KL term of the VAE projector. Result: averages 0.924 (cross-entropy, mean), 0.927 (evidential, mean) and 0.938 (evidential, Dempster-Shafer); removing either projector loss gives 0.921-0.922.

Check that the result is not tied to the backbone or fragile to image degradation. Setup: swap CLIP ViT-L/14 for CLIP ViT-B/16 and for DINOv2-L; separately apply block-wise distortion, contrast change and JPEG compression at five severity levels against Effort, Face X-ray, PatchForensics, SBI, FWA, LipForensics and FTCN. Result: the smaller CLIP backbone averages 0.829 and DINOv2 0.808 against 0.938, so the gains depend on a large text-image backbone; under perturbations the method stays above 99% AUC at every severity while pixel-artifact detectors drop sharply under JPEG, and it is more stable than Effort at high severity. Trainable parameters 0.868M (Effort 0.199M, GenD 0.104M), 47.4 frames per second.

Check that uncertainty flags errors. Setup: on FaceForensics++ and the unseen Celeb-DF v2, DFDC and DFD, plot the fused uncertainty separately for correct and incorrect predictions, and plot accuracy against the fraction of most-uncertain samples rejected, compared with the deterministic baseline. Result: correct predictions cluster near zero uncertainty and misclassifications mostly at high uncertainty; accuracy rises monotonically as more uncertain samples are rejected and stays above the baseline curve, with a large gain on DFD from rejecting only the top 10%.

Measure calibration against a deterministic version of the same model. Setup: expected calibration error on Celeb-DF v2, DFD and MobileFaceSwap for the cross-entropy, mean-fusion variant and for the full model. Result: 0.13 / 0.15 / 0.19 (average 0.16) for the deterministic variant against 0.07 / 0.07 / 0.08 (average 0.07).

notes: Robustness to perturbations is reported only as a figure; the >99% AUC statement is the paper's text, test set not specified.
